title: This Prehistoric Creature is the Only Ocean-Dwelling Amphibian Ever Discovered - Nautilus
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontologyThis Prehistoric Creature is the Only Ocean-Dwelling Amphibian Ever DiscoveredIt lived in the Triassic muck on the seafloorJCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CDT on October 27, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe crab-eating frog survives by holding its pee (sort of). By retaining urea, the nitrogenous waste compound expelled in urine, this frog prevents water loss via osmosis, which allows it to survive prolonged periods in saltwater. This neat little trick makes it one of the only known amphibians capable of living in a brackish environment. Until now. New research by a team of Chinese and American paleontologists details the discovery of the first fully marine amphibian in China’s Guizhou Province. Their analysis is based on two nearly complete skeletons dating to around 240 million years ago during the Triassic period. According to the team, the species (Gerrothorax maritimus) was around three feet long, disc-shaped, and likely an oceanic bottom-dweller. Its most remarkable feature was bony armor on its back, likely a defense against the many ichthyosaurs swimming in the Triassic oceans. Read more: “How ‘Useless’ Science Unraveled an Amphibian Apocalypse”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
